title: Cross-pop routing safety gate and graceful model-variant fallback
creator: Aisha Tan
description: Goal: Implement a cross-PoP (POP = point-of-presence / region) safety gate that fuses latency percentiles (p50/p95) and a compact network-health score to decide region preference and trigger graceful fallback to compatible model variants or lower tiers.
background: We currently route by simple latency thresholds per POP but lack an integrated signal for transient network degradation and variant compatibility. Recent incidents showed oscillation when a POP had low p50 but high packet loss spikes, causing increased tail latency for some customers. We need a robust scoring + safety gate to avoid thrash and ensure predictable failovers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New scoring function produces a ranked list of candidate POPs for a sample workload and matches experimental gold-standard scoring on historical telemetry; 2) Safety gate prevents routing to POPs that exceed packet-loss or connection-error budget for >2 minutes; 3) Fallback map selects a compatible model variant with the same API surface and acceptable quality degradation; 4) End-to-end canary shows <1% error increase and no customer-facing latency spike during controlled switchovers; 5) Console dashboard exposes per-route score, windowed p50/p95, and network-health contribution.
design_notes:
- Combine p50 and p95 using weighted fusion: score_latency = 0.6 * normalized_p95 + 0.4 * normalized_p50 after applying percentile smoothing (EWMA with alpha=0.15).
- Network health index computed as weighted sum of packet_loss_rate, tcp_retransmit_rate, and mean_conn_reset_rate with short-window (30s) and long-window (5m) components.
- Final POP score = score_latency * latency_weight + (1 - network_penalty) * network_weight with configurable weights per customer tier.
- Introduce safety gate states: OK, Degraded, Isolated. Transition hysteresis: require sustained violation for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (30s windows) before marking Degraded, and 3 windows before Isolated.
- Map incompatible models to fallback variants via a compatibility matrix; fallbacks must preserve tokenization and function-calling schema where possible.
implementation_plan:
1) Telemetry: add short-window metrics to the region-telemetry stream and a derived aggregating job for p50/p95 + health components. 2) Scoring service: new lightweight scorer service in control plane that exposes /score(route, candidate_pops) -> ranked list + reason codes. 3) Router integration: consult scorer on every routing decision; cache scores for 15s by default, per-route TTL policy for high-priority routes. 4) Fallback selection: implement variant-resolver with staged compatibility checks. 5) Feature flag and canary: rollout to 5% of non-critical traffic then ramp.
- Estimated work split: telemetry (2), scorer (3), router integration (2), variant resolver (1).
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive short-window detection reduces exposure time but increases false positives; balanced using EWMA and hysteresis.
- Caching scores improves throughput but delays reaction; choose per-route TTL based on SLO.
- Using a composite score simplifies decisioning but may obscure individual signal failures; expose reason codes to the console.
- Fallbacking to smaller quantized variants reduces cost/latency but may degrade output quality for some prompts; map fallbacks conservatively and surface quality delta metrics.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for scoring math and hysteresis state machine.
- Integration test harness that replays historical telemetry from 2026-02 incidents and asserts routing choices match expected safe behavior.
- Load test with synthetic packet-loss patterns to verify router stability and score cache TTL behavior.
- Canary: staged rollout on low-risk customer group with A/B comparison for token cost and output quality metrics.
rollout_plan:
1) Internally gate under FF 'cross_pop_safety_v1' and enable scorer only for internal routes. 2) Canary: enable for 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor errors and latency. 3) Ramp to 25% for 72h, validate data. 4) Full enable with monitoring alerts and automatic rollback on SLO breach.
- Rollback plan: revert scorer usage and purge TTL cache to resume old behavior; automated rollback if p95 increases >20% vs baseline.
monitoring:
- Console dashboard: route-level score, p50/p95 windows (30s, 5m), network-health components, safety-gate state timeline.
- Alerts: safety_gate_entered_degraded (>=2 consecutive windows) and safety_gate_isolated (>=3 windows).
- Quality regression alert tied to eval prompt set: quality_delta > 3% for fallback variant triggers immediate rollback.
- Observability links attached to ticket.
